key_insight: General-purpose LLMs outperform domain-specific pretrained models in the reported alloy-property benchmarks, with further gains from numerical predictions supplied as prompts.
engineering_relevance: Combining existing property predictors with general-purpose LLMs could improve alloy screening while reducing reliance on expensive domain-specific pretraining.
method: Benchmark general-purpose LLMs against SteelBERT, MatSciBERT, and SciBERT across Ti, steels, high-entropy alloys, and Al.
Prompt DeepSeek V3.1 and Gemini-2.5-Flash with CatBoost or SteelBERT predictions to guide corrections.
Compare similarity-selected reference data subsets and assess self-reported prediction confidence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that using only 5% high-similarity training references yields performance similar to using the full training set, while hybrid predictions outperform both prior models and unguided LLMs.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical error metrics or detailed out-of-distribution results, so robustness on substantially different alloys remains unclear.
paper_title: Quantifying out-of-distribution data severity with Wasserstein distances: benchmarking large language models for alloy property prediction
